correctness.rationale: On \(E:y^2=x^3-1\), addition by \(T=(0,i)\) gives the exact identity \(x(P)x(P+T)x(P-T)=4\). The divisor valuation matrix of each H-coset has columns (−2,1,1),(1,−2,1),(1,1,−2); two-column minor 3 is invertible modulo every allowed m. Each complete coset gives exactly one constant Kummer relation and no other relation occurs because different cosets have disjoint divisor supports. Kummer theory therefore gives \(m^t\) normalized components of degree \(m^{r-t}\), with Galois group \((\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^{r-t}\). Riemann–Hurwitz over E and three fully m-ramified points per occupied coset yields \(1+\frac{3c}{2}m^{r-t-1}(m-1)\). The exact SymPy checker was executed successfully, confirming the identity and finite sample modular kernels. The proof, not sample arithmetic, covers all allowed m,r and distinct shifts.

value.rationale: The separated-shift hypothesis is a natural geometric restriction in the motivating construction of complete curves in moduli. The excluded three-torsion collisions are an entire geometric boundary stratum, not an arbitrary special parameter choice. An occupied coset changes branch support; a full coset introduces a hidden norm relation and physically separates the normalization into m components. The precise component count, Galois group and genus for every occupancy pattern supply usable structural invariants of these parameter curves and explain a sharp and sometimes dramatic departure from the generic formula.
